tasks.title: Extend SessionApi and MCP surface to expose new phases, read/advance operations, and human-approval gate
acceptance_criteria: ngv2.session_api.SessionApi is additively extended to support new lifecycle phases ('source' -> ... -> 'done') and 'manual_review' state.
SessionApi exposes get_current_phase(session_id) returning the phase string.
SessionApi exposes get_parked_package(session_id) returning the parked submission package dict or None.
SessionApi exposes get_readiness_reason(session_id) returning the missing artifact reason string or None.
SessionApi exposes advance(session_id, approval_decision=None) to drive autonomous transitions, gating the awaiting_submission -> submitted transition.
The transition from awaiting_submission to submitted requires an operator approval decision that approves the submission.
session_mcp.py is updated to export get_current_phase, get_parked_package, get_readiness_reason, and advance as tools.
All extensions are pure, deterministic, and perform no network, wall-clock, randomness, or subprocess calls.
tasks.verification_command: python -c "from ngv2.session_api import SessionApi; from ngv2.session_mcp import build_tools; print('Imports and tool builders are valid!')"

spec.objective: Additively extend SessionApi and its MCP surface to expose the new phases and read/advance operations while gating the awaiting_submission -> submitted step behind the injected human-approval seam.
functional_requirements: Extend SessionApi to support all phases in source -> hunt -> triage -> verify -> poc -> detonate -> novelty -> report -> awaiting_submission -> submitted -> done, plus manual_review.
Implement get_current_phase(session_id) to retrieve the current phase from the session pipeline data.
Implement get_parked_package(session_id) to return the parked turn-in-ready package dict if present in the session.
Implement get_readiness_reason(session_id) using ngv2.submission_readiness_gate.readiness to return the missing artifact reason or None.
Implement advance(session_id, approval_decision=None) to run autonomous transitions in a loop until halting at awaiting_submission or done, or failing a gate.
Gate the transition from awaiting_submission to submitted behind an approval_decision check using ngv2.human_approval_gate.
Expose the four new operations (get_current_phase, get_parked_package, get_readiness_reason, advance) as tools in session_mcp.py build_tools.
Ensure the entire implementation is pure, deterministic, and free of I/O, network, or subprocesses, importing only stdlib and ngv2 modules.
spec.interfaces: Exposes get_current_phase(session_id) -> str, get_parked_package(session_id) -> dict|None, get_readiness_reason(session_id) -> str|None, advance(session_id, approval_decision=None) -> dict. Update build_tools(api: SessionApi) -> Dict[str, Callable].
edge_cases: A session without any artifacts returns a valid readiness reason indicating 'confidence' or another appropriate initial missing artifact.
An invalid or non-existent session_id returns a 404 dict for all read and advance operations.
Calling advance on a session parked in awaiting_submission without a valid approval decision returns a dict indicating that it remains parked.
Simultaneous failures are resolved via the readiness gate precedence.
non_goals: Do not define or modify FSM transition rules or gate logic (consume ngv2_lifecycle_fsm_wiring).
Do not implement a live platform turn-in adapter or UI components.
Do not perform wall-clock or random queries.
spec.implementation_notes:
Load the session data, retrieve the artifacts, call the corresponding pure gate functions from state_machine, session_gate, submission_readiness_gate, and human_approval_gate. When transitioning to report or awaiting_submission, build and store the submission package in the session data JSON. In session_mcp.py, expand the returned dict from build_tools to include the new tool handlers.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Uses the real SessionDB, state_machine, session_gate, contracts, and sibling gates from NobleGreedv2.

token_budget_ratio.note: Balanced implementation and test budget to cover the new methods and MCP tool integrations.
